record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README text only; code and referenced research files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports weight edits based on harmful/harmless residual directions and refusal outcomes in released models. This tests practical direction-based removal, but uses norm-preserving biprojection and, for the MoE model, expert-granular edits rather than the original activation ablation.
record.gate_note: README reports refusal rates after abliterating five Gemma 4 models, plus a dense-only versus EGA comparison for the MoE model. The README also reports KL divergence values. The 4-bit-versus-bf16 direction cosine and task-vector result do not test the claim's refusal direction and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal rates after converting harmful-minus-harmless residual directions into weight edits on five released Gemma 4 instruct models. That bears directly on V2. It uses norm-preserving biprojection with per-layer directions, plus expert-slice edits for the MoE model, rather than the original single-direction ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims biprojection plus EGA gives 'sub-1% refusal rate across all models', which conflicts with its own table (12B 2.0%, 31B 3.2%). It also claims larger models absorb abliteration better (lower KL), that MoE experts carry most of the refusal signal, and that the Unified 12B needs only its upper 70% of layers edited.
record.recipe_differences: This is an abliteration research/tool repository, not a stated replication. It computes per-layer directions from 800 harmful/harmless prompt residuals and edits weights with norm-preserving biprojection; the MoE method additionally edits expert slices. It does not use the original single-direction activation ablation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Model architecture changes the procedure: the 12B Unified model uses only the top 70% of layers, and 26B-A4B requires EGA in addition to dense-pathway editing for the reported lower refusal count.

fits_no_version.finding: Directions computed on the 4-bit model match bf16 directions (mean cosine 0.935) and are used for the 31B export.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal directions are stable under weight quantization of the same model.

fits_no_version.finding: Default keyword refusal markers ('illegal', 'harmful') match disclaimers, not refusals, inflating refusal counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reported post-abliteration refusal rates depend on the refusal-judging method.

record.problems: This is README-reported evidence only; code and result files were not inspected. The README gives no pre-edit refusal baselines for the five-model table, no uncertainty estimates, and no general capability benchmark. It reports that most flagged refusals were refusal-then-comply false positives but does not provide corrected rates. KL references are unspecified.
record.rows_left_out: No reported refusal or KL results were left out. The README's 4-bit direction cosine result and task-vector negation result do not directly measure the claim's refusal direction or refusal behavior.

untested.parts: Pre-edit refusal rates for the five models, and capability retention beyond unreferenced KL values. sanity_check.py results are not reported in the README.
Not tested. Per-layer directions and expert-slice edits are not a comparison of affine, cone or multi-direction descriptions.
Not tested. No single-direction activation ablation, no induction of refusal by adding the direction, no harmless-refusal or capability checks.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is README-only. No uncertainty is reported, and there are no pre-edit baselines. Low post-edit refusal on harmful benchmarks for instruct models is read as removal. The V4 link in the record was dropped: EGA reuses the same direction per expert. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The README describes per-layer directions and weight edits, not a single direction ablated at every layer and position or added to induce refusals. It does not report harmless-request refusal outcomes or general capability results.
The README does not report pre-edit refusal rates for the released model results, nor a full assessment of capabilities after editing.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against ablation is reported.

The README reports expert-granular versus dense-only results for one MoE model, but does not test affine or cone geometry or compare a dominant direction with additional directions across the model family.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are measured.
The models are edited separately; transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is not reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

source_check.notes: This repo looks like a copy of TrevorJS's work: all HF links are TrevorJS models, it was created and last pushed within 10 minutes, and it has 0 stars. Count it with gh:trevors/gemma-4-abliteration as one source, not independent evidence. The README's 'sub-1% across all models' contradicts its own table (12B 2.0%, 31B 3.2%), and it gives no unedited refusal rates. The pack's verdicts carried no [lN] ids, so l1 and l2 are positional.

statements.correction: Gemma 4 26B-A4B: dense-only abliteration leaves 29/100 refusals; adding EGA on 128 expert down_proj slices per layer gives 3/100. Same results and TrevorJS model links as gh:trevors.
statements.problem: Numbers right for this study. But the text's HF links all point to TrevorJS models, so this repo seems to mirror gh:trevors/gemma-4-abliteration; listing both reads as two sources for one result.
